questions.prompt: Why is DNS called an application but also infrastructure?
options: It's an application-layer protocol, but nearly every other application depends on it

questions.prompt: Which transport does an ordinary DNS lookup use, and when does DNS switch to the other?
options: UDP port 53; TCP for zone transfers and answers too big for one packet
TCP port 53; UDP for zone transfers

questions.prompt: In `ftp.cs.marshall.edu.`, which part is the second-level domain?
How does the `edu` registry make `marshall.edu` someone else's job?
options: With NS records that delegate it to Marshall's nameservers
It copies Marshall's zone each night

questions.prompt: Which record type is matched with the right job?
options: CNAME: makes one name an alias for another
MX: maps an address back to a name

questions.prompt: A domain has `MX 5 a.example.com.` and `MX 15 b.example.com.`. What happens when a.example.com is down?
options: Senders fall back to b, the higher-numbered backup
Senders try the A record of example.com

questions.prompt: What's the reverse lookup name for 203.0.113.25? (the full name)
Which SOA field must you increase after every change, or the secondaries won't copy it?
A secondary can't reach its primary. What decides how long it keeps answering for the zone?
Which two things does DNS client software need?
options: The root key and a port
The FQDN and a nameserver's IP address
A MAC address and the default gateway

questions.prompt: Which resolver field lists servers from a configuration file, used when the resolver knows nothing better?
During a lookup, a server replies with a referral. What does the resolver do?
options: Caches the delegation and chooses new servers closer to the answer
Returns an error to the client

questions.prompt: A resolver with an empty cache looks up `www.example.org`. Which servers does it ask, in order?
options: The root, then a .org server, then example.org's server

questions.prompt: In a DNS response, what does the AA flag mean?
options: The answer came from a server authoritative for the zone

questions.prompt: Which QTYPE copies an entire zone?
Why are caching servers a favorite target?
options: One poisoned entry misleads every client that uses the server until the TTL runs out

questions.prompt: Many sites announce the same prefix with BGP, so each user's queries reach the nearest copy. What is it?
`dig mx example.com` shows status NOERROR, ANSWER: 0, and an SOA in the authority section. What does it mean?
options: The name exists but has no MX records

questions.prompt: What does DNSSEC protect, and what doesn't it?
options: It encrypts queries but doesn't sign them
It proves answers are genuine and unchanged, but doesn't hide which names you look up
It stops DDoS attacks but not poisoning

questions.prompt: nslookup is the newer tool and gives more information than dig.
A name can have several A records.
Which record type holds the zone's serial number and refresh timers? (three letters)
Name the attack where malware hides stolen data inside DNS query names to get it past a firewall. (two words)
